text:
Maya R: @channel paging: spike in 5xx for inference traffic from EU regions and smart-routing showing repeated fallbacks to a wrong variant. Alerting customers noticing errors. IncBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1427 — high error-rate on smart-routing fallbacks (auto-paged oncall). Samir Patel: acked, I'm oncall. First goal: identify whether this is routing policy misconfig or DNS/edge stale endpoints. Any recent deploys to routing or variant mapping? Maya R: Routing policy diff from last night shows a new fallback rule that maps incompatible model-quantized-v1 as compatible fallback for gpt-like families — suspect. Lee Tran: seeing lots of CONNECT failures at edge and a bunch of requests hitting an older edge IP that shouldn't be advertised anymore. Running quick dig: ```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
eu1.example-edge.redwood.ai. 3600 IN A 52.12.34.56
``` That 3600 TTL is not what we expect (should be 60). NetOps Bot: Last RR-set change committed 2026-03-14T21:15Z, TTL 3600. Nadia Gomez: that TTL explains propagation delay. Some regions still resolve to decommissioned endpoints which return 502/503 or route to a variant that doesn't support current KV cache layout -> 500s. Samir Patel: can we confirm logs that show model variant mismatch causing 500s? Lee Tran: yes, sample from router logs: ```
2026-03-15T02:04:12Z router-eu request_id=abc123 route=eu-west fallback_variant=model-quantized-v1 error=kernel-mismatch runtime_error="kv_cache_missing"
``` Maya R: customer impact: partial failures and increased latency for EU customers — roughly 8-12% error rate for eu-west for last 12 minutes. Escalate to NetOps and Runtime. Nadia Gomez: on it — will check Route53/edge record TTLs and rollback option to previous RR-set. Quick mitigation plan: 1) Disable smart-routing fallback to stop mapping to the wrong variant 2) Lower DNS TTL for affected record sets to 60 and push new RR-set 3) Purge edge cache / CDN 4) Roll back routing policy commit if needed Samir Patel: I'll implement 1 and 4 via the control plane — applying a temporary policy that forces strict-region routing and removes cross-variant fallback. Command I will run: ```bash
# save current policy
rictl routing export --env prod > /tmp/routing-before.json
# apply emergency strict policy
rictl routing patch --env prod --json '{"smart_routing": {"fallback": false, "region_preference": "strict"}}'
``` Maya R: go for it, please log the change id. Samir Patel: applied patch, change_id=chg_0a9f3b. Policy now: fallback disabled, region_preference=strict. Monitoring... Lee Tran: confirmed drop in fallback attempts in router logs. Error rate trending down but DNS still inconsistent. Nadia Gomez: I've submitted route53 change to set TTL=60 and point RR-set to current healthy edge IPs. Change ID: /change/C123456789. Command: ```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"eu1.example-edge.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.98.76.54"}]}}]}'
``` NetOps Bot: change queued, propagation expected within TTL but some resolvers may cache longer. Purge push to CDN: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://edge-api.redwood.ai/v1/purge" -H "Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_TOKEN" -d '{"hosts":["eu1.example-edge.redwood.ai"]}'
``` Lee Tran: CDN purge acknowledged. Immediate impact: error rate down to ~2% in eu-west, latency back within SLO for most requests. Maya R: OK, next — we suspect the upstream change that introduced the wrong fallback was a bad mapping in model-compatibility table. Samir Patel: found PR #4123 merged 2026-03-14 20:58Z altered compatibility matrix. Reverting that commit should restore previous fallback mapping. I will create rollback PR to staging and promote to prod later after validation. Change queued as chg_0a9f3b-rollback. Nadia Gomez: still seeing a handful of clients hitting stale IPs (likely corporate resolvers). We'll monitor DNS query patterns and reach out to major affected customers if needed. Action: NetOps to run glue refresh with edns0 to push new RR-set. NetOps Bot: running glue refresh now. Samir Patel: monitoring routing-level metrics — fallbacks suppressed, service errors decreasing. Maya R: customer impact summary for pager/responses: - Time window: 02:03–02:22 UTC - Affected region: EU (primary eu-west) - Peak error-rate: ~12% - Impact: degraded inference results (500s) for ~8% of EU requests, some increased latency for additional ~5% - Major customers affected: flagged Acme Internal (support ticket opened), NovaApps (SRE notified) - No data exfiltration, no model data loss Samir Patel: adding temporary alert threshold for eu-west to 3% errors for next 6 hours and paging silence after 30m if stabilized. ```bash
rictl alerts update --env prod --alert-id eu-west-error --threshold 3 --window 5m --snooze 30m
``` Lee Tran: logs show no more kernel-mismatch errors after policy patch. Margin of safety: keep fallback disabled until we validate compatibility changes. Nadia Gomez: follow-ups for tomorrow shift: 1) roll forward or fixcompat matrix PR to ensure correct variant mapping 2) confirm TTL remains 60 for 24h, then increase gradually 3) reach out to major affected customers with RCA/mitigation note 4) prepare postmortem and incident timeline Samir Patel: preparing handoff note for rotation to night squad (oncall at 03:00 UTC). Handoff summary: mitigation applied (fallback disabled, DNS TTL lowered, CDN purge), error rate down to ~1.5%, tasks: validate rollback of compat PR, monitor DNS resolver TTLs, contact support for customer outreach. Maya R: tagging @Nadia @Samir — please update this thread with any change IDs and final RCA link. Also file incident ticket INC-2026-1427 in tracker when stable. Samir Patel: final change ids: routing-patch=chg_0a9f3b, route53-change=/change/C123456789, rollback-pr=PR#4130 (draft). I'll follow up with postmortem. IncBot: Incident INC-2026-1427 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Reaction: :white_check_mark:
